appeal.letter:
Subject: Appeal Against Denial of Claim ID 5c8956ba-3359-155e-be7a-3366d080341a – Pre‑Existing Disease Waiting Period  

Claim Details:  
Patient: Tijuana Allena Nolan (ID 5c8956ba-3359-155e-a6f4-0e1d5bc43a77)  
Date of Service: 2024-11-02  
Procedure: New York Heart Association Functional Classification panel (cardiac)  
Diagnosis: Chronic congestive heart failure  
Policy: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Plan Code SGH‑GOLD) – Coverage effective 2023-01-07  
Claim Amount: INR 49,054.56  

Grounds for Appeal:  
The diagnosis of chronic congestive heart failure was first made on 2024-11-02, which is after the policy start date of 2023‑01‑07. Under the policy definition, a condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is not a Pre‑Existing Disease [suraksha_gold_policy#5].  

Accordingly, the Pre‑Existing Disease waiting period does not apply to this condition, because the waiting‑period clause is triggered only for conditions that meet the definition of Pre‑Existing Disease [suraksha_gold_policy#10].  

Furthermore, the insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period is applicable. No documentary evidence has been provided to show that the heart failure was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date, as required by the claims procedure [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6].  

Clinical Necessity:  
The treating cardiologist will attach detailed clinical notes confirming that the New York Heart Association Functional Classification panel is essential for the ongoing management and risk stratification of the patient’s chronic congestive heart failure.  

Denial Standards and Appeal Rights:  
The insurer’s grievance cell must acknowledge this appeal within three working days and render a decision within fifteen days, as stipulated in the appeals and grievance procedures [claims_procedure_and_grievance#8][claims_procedure_and_grievance#9].  

Specific Request:  
In view of the foregoing, we respectfully request that the denial be withdrawn, the claim be re‑processed, and the amount of INR 49,054.56 be paid promptly. If any delay has occurred due to the initial denial, interest for the period of delay should be applied as per the policy provisions.  

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.  

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (Clause 2.2) are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C4. Appeals and Grievances > C4.2 Timelines
citations.quote:
### C4.2 Timelines
The insurer's grievance cell must acknowledge an appeal within 3 working days and decide it within 15 days. If the denial is overturned, the claim must be paid with interest for the period of delay.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C4. Appeals and Grievances > C4.1 Right to Appeal
citations.quote:
## C4. Appeals and Grievances  
### C4.1 Right to Appeal
The insured, or the provider on the insured's behalf, may appeal a denial in writing within 30 days of the denial letter. The appeal should identify the claim, the denial reason, the policy clauses relied upon and the supporting clinical evidence.
